truthRule: Audience templates adapt framing, vocabulary, pacing, evidence depth and CTA; they never fork the factual core.

templates.goal: Enable architecture, security and implementation scrutiny.
templates.cta: Inspect the receipt or offer a counterexample.
templates.passExample: Show the invalidated DAG nodes, selected checks and authoritative comparator.
templates.failExample: A card that says verification is smarter.

templates.goal: Support a bounded adoption or risk decision.
templates.cta: Decide whether the bounded pilot merits evaluation.
templates.passExample: Show the authority boundary first, then the receipt and residual risk.
templates.failExample: Lead with class names and omit operational consequences.

templates.goal: Make setup, observation, failure and rollback realistic.
templates.cta: Run the read-only preflight and inspect the receipt.
templates.passExample: Show setup, observable success, denied write and rollback marker.
templates.failExample: Say easy to deploy without steps or failure signals.

templates.goal: Build a truthful mental model with minimal jargon.
templates.cta: Explore the bounded example and its limits.
antiPatterns: cute analogy that changes the truth
templates.passExample: Use a doorway analogy, then show the real permission flow and receipt.
templates.failExample: Replace the actual boundary with a cartoon lock.

templates.goal: Make a safe extension path and evidence expectations obvious.
templates.cta: Prepare and validate an evidence bundle; submission remains a separate action.
templates.passExample: Prepare, validate and package evidence, then stop before submit.
templates.failExample: Animate a pull request merge after local validation.
